DILG Legal Opinion No. 11 S. 2016 1 8 FEB City of Escalante, Negros Occidental Dear Acting Vice-Mayor Escala: This has reference to your letter dated 26 January 2016 referring to the Department, for review and legal opinion, a copy of the draft Resolution of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Escalante entitled "A RESOLUTION TO CONCUR THE APPOINTMENT OF MR. ALBERTO O. ABIBAS, JR., AS CITY ADMINISTRATOR EFFECTIVE JANUARY 22, 2016." Based on your letter as well as its attachments, Mr. Alberto O. Abibas, Jr. is one of the respondents in OMB-V-A-14-0183 entitled "Office of the Ombudsman-Visayas, Regional Office VI-Field Investigation Office Represented by: Ronaldo S. Amador, et al. vs. Celestino M. Sembrano, et (All of Escalante, Negros Occidental) for dishonesty. On 09 December 2015, the Office of the Ombudsman rendered a Decision (approved by Hon. Conchita Carpio Morales, Ombudsman, on 18 December 2015) in the aforesaid case finding respondent Abibas and several others guilty of Dishonesty and Falsification and meting upon them the penalty of dismissal from the service, including the accessory penalties of cancellation of civil service eligibility, forfeiture of retirement benefits, and the perpetual disqualification for re-employment and/or re-election in the government service. In the event that the penalty of dismissal from the service can no longer be enforced due to respondents' separation from the service, the same Ombudsman Decision provides that the principal penalty of dismissal be converted into a fine in an amount equivalent to respondents' last salary for one year payable to the Office of the Ombudsman, and may be deductible from respondents' retirement benefits, accrued leave credits or any receivable from his/her office. The City Mayor of Escalante City or his authorized representative was the one directed in the aforesaid Ombudsman Decision to implement the penalty of dismissal as well as its accessory penalties against respondent Abibas and several others. Thereafter, the Acting Mayor of Escalante City appointed Abibas as City Administrator effective 22 January 2016. Said appointment is now subject to concurrence by the Sangguniang Panlungsod.

Hence, your letter-request. At the outset, may we invite your attention to Section 454 of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991, thus: "Section 454. Officials of the City. -n (a) There shall be in each city a mayor, a vice-mayor, sangguniang panlungsod members, a secretary to the sangguniang pan/ungsod, a city treasurer, a city assessor, a city accountant, a city budget officer, a city planning and development coordinator, a city engineer, a city health officer, a city civil registrar, a_city administrator, a city legal officer, a city veterinarian, a city social welfare and development officer, and a city genera/ services officer. (d) Unless otherwise provided herein, heads of' depurtments and offices shall be appointed by the city mayor with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniangpanlungsod members. subject to civil service law rules and regulaÜOO$. The sangguniang panlungsod shall act on the appointment within fifteen (15) days from the date of its submission, otherwise the same shall be deemed confirmed. As could be gleaned from the foregoing, appointment of a City Administrptor by the City Mayor requires concurrence by the Sangguniang Panlungsod. The Department has consistently opined that the power to concur of the sangguniang panlungsod mentioned in the aforequoted provision of the Local Government Code of 1991 is intended to determine whether or not the appointee of the City Mayor possesses all the qualifications prescribed for the position under Section 480 (a)l of the Local Government Code of 1991 and none of the disqualifications provided for by existing laws. Section 480. Qualifications, Terms, Powers and Duties. (a) No person shall be appointed administrator unless he is a citizen of the Philippines, a resident of the local government unit concerned, of good moral character, a holder of a college degree pwferably in public administration, law, or any other related course from a recognized college or university, and a first grade civil service eligible or its equivalent. Ile must have acquired experience in management and administration work for at least five (5) years in the case of the provincial or city administrator, and three (3) years in the case of the municipal administrator. The term of administrator is coterminous with that of his appointing authority. The appointment of an administrator shall be mandatory for the provincial and city governments, and optional for the municipal governmenL

Let it be noted that in the Decision rendered by thc Office of the Ombudsman in OMB-V•14-0183, Abibas, among others, were meted the penalty of dismissal from the service as well as its accessory penalties, such as cancellation of civil service eligibility and perpetual disqualification for re-employment and/or re-election in the government service. The cancellation of Abibas' civil service eligibility, in effect, means that he already lacks the required civil service eligibility for a City Administrator enumerated under the aforesaid Section 480 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991. Hence, he does not meet all the qualifications for a City Administrator enumerated under the Code. On the other hand, the accessory penalty of perpetual disqualification Ibr re- employment in the government service, in effect, precludes him from holding any appointive or even elective office in the government. Unless Abibas obtained a Temporary Restraining Order (T RO) or other favorable reliefs from the court of competent jurisdiction, Abibas is disqualified to bc appointed as City Administrator since Section 27 (I) of Republic Act No. 6770 or the Ombudsman Act of 1989, as reiterated in Administrative Order No. 7 (Ombudsman Rules of Procedure) and ONIB Memorandum Circular No. 01, series of 2006, states that the decision of Office of the Ombudsman is immediately executory and may not bc interrupted by any motion, appeal or petition that may be filed by the respondents. Moreover, the refusal or failure by any officer without just cause to comply with an order of the Oflice of the Ombudsman to remove, suspend, demote, fine or censure shall be a ground for disciplinary action against said officer. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Is/17 Copy furnished: DIR. MARGIE A. BILIGAN Officer-in-Charge, DILG-Negros Island Region Negros Occidental Provincial Office PAC Bldg.
